recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-7348 unless PA later reopens the Appointment participant invariant or actor cardinality policy.
issue_request: FHIR-7348 asked to make Appointment.participant.actor 1..1. It was Published with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification: keep actor optional, add an invariant requiring either participant.type and/or participant.actor, and document use cases where actor can be null.
initial_application: No current-history commit explicitly names FHIR-7348, but 44a2cf49 added Appointment narrative explaining an unknown actor with participant type and added the Appointment.participant invariant in the spreadsheet source. Later commits af77b9dac9, 329acfd730, and 33b409a4b6 preserved the rule while converting the expression to FHIRPath, changing MUST to SHALL, and moving to current StructureDefinition source.
additional_context: Appointment is active in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition keeps Appointment.participant.actor at 0..1 and applies app-1 to participant.type and participant.actor with expression type.exists() or actor.exists(). Current narrative and element comments explain the unknown-actor scheduling use case. Later related Jira hits FHIR-28588 and FHIR-34141 concerned CareTeam targeting and value-set wording and did not reverse the FHIR-7348 invariant.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The combined branch received an empty audit commit because the active source already matches the final Jira disposition and making actor mandatory would be incorrect.
